If you don’t have to get an ultrasound early- just don’t

3 weeks ago I found out I was expecting. I’ve had three miscarriages in the course of a year and I’m super high alert. At 4 weeks I started having sharp pain. I have a history of ovarian cyst so I went to the er to check it out. They found an irregular gestational sac with no yolk sac or fetal pole. Diagnosis: suspected ectopic pregnancy. Hcg:456 

I went back two days later where the did a repeat blood. Hcg: 989 

Flash forward to week 5.5 the paid intensified. I rushed over to the er due to being unable to walk. Hcg: 20,000
Ultrasound: the irregular sac corrected itself and a yolk sac was present but no fetal pole. 

The ob sac on call came down to my bed and advised we do an emergency d&c as it is most likely life threatening. 

I refused and demanded she show what evidence she had to which she walked away. 

She came back and said the d&c was not necessary, but she recommends I perform a medical abortion since it’s obviously a missed miscarriage since no fetal pole formed. I again refused and told her I would prefer my body to do what it needs to do naturally. This is not my first rodeo. 

Today-6 weeks 5 days ultrasound: a perfect little bean with a strong heart beat flickering away 

Moral of the story: skip the early ultrasound and always always always trust your intuition

I have held my breath for the past 3 weeks. Tonight I can breath 

Edit to add: sometimes an early ultrasound is medically necessary. As mentioned in the thread, If you or your doctor suspect something is wrong please do get an ultrasound. Always get a second opinion if you feel as though the diagnosis may be inaccurate. ❤️‍🩹

For over a decade I battled with infertility. I watched my friends grow more and more distant because of their growing families. I missed baby showers and first birthdays, playdate get-togethers and walks through the park. People shy away from sharing these moments with an infertile girl.
It's human nature to protect. I watched my friends change. There isn't really much you can say to a woman who can't have any children. You feel sorry. You tell them not to worry, it will happen when you stop trying. You tell them about this one girl you know, who knows a girl, who was trying for so long, then adopted and then had a child when they stopped trying. You try to be kind. But its all horse pucky and it all hurts. There is no elegant way to be nice and not hurt at the same time. It doesn't exist.

Infertility cost me my first marriage. After a decade of trying to conceive, I started resenting him, his closeness and caring and detachment. I started resenting having sex with him, it became a symbol of our failures. I hated him. He hated me. So I left. It was the best decision i could have made for our happiness.

I am newly married, just days since our very intimate pandemic wedding. I am a new woman. He looks at me with passion, touches with desire, admires me for everything that I know I am...and used to be years ago. I am a woman.

7 days into our marriage we got our BFP. Strong, thick pink line... body raging with  sore boobs, bloated belly and  the joy of all the symptoms that prove life is there. I am in love. I am scared. I don't know how to do this again.

Hope is a horrible thing for infertility. Hope kills. Hope destroys. One of my angel babies was lost at 21w3d. A perfect little human. I had picked out my  nursery colors that time. I even bought some tiny newborn clothes. I dared to hope.

4 weeks and 2 days and I don't know how to do this. Dare I hope again? Will it destroy me again? Is this the one? Dare I think about nursery colors? Dare I join a group of pregnant ladies? Am I ready to erase my existence once again if hope betrays me one more time?

Ranting. Venting. Sharing. I know I'm not alone, but infertility is lonely business. To whoever needs to hear it - you are enough. You always have been and you always will be. You matter more than your womb. Love yourself first. Always.

I became concerned it was ectopic, because I was on the copper IUD and was told its common for pregnancies to be ectopic while on it. Google said ectopic pregnancies can take 10-15 weeks to show on a test. So when I started having really sharp pains on my left side just like my last ectopic pregnancy, I went straight to the ER.

They did bloodwork, an ultrasound, a CT scan and... nothing. My HCG value was 1: not pregnant.

I was so confused. I've never been so certain I was pregnant and been wrong.

Well, for the next month the bleeding never fully stopped. I spotted all through November until my period (again 2 days late) started.

During this period, which was very heavy and painful, I passed a white clot of some sort. I reached out to my doctor, she told me to take a pregnancy test and it was positive. It was the weekend when I got the positive test, so I had to wait until Monday to get a hold of my doctors. I took a second test Monday morning to see if the line was darker or lighter, becausemy friend kept telling me how she was having regular periods when she was pregnant with her fifth child, so I could very well still be pregnant. The line seemed just a tad bit darker.

I wasn't able to come in until Tuesday, where they did an ultrasound and a pee test. And again, they found NOTHING. My pee test was negative and scans showed nothing. The doctor kept talking to me like a child and calling it irregular bleeding instead of a miscarriage. I was like "it's not possible to have two false positive tests in a row!" And she indignantly replied, "yes, it is." 
I will say, my urine gets very diluted during the day because I drink a lot of water. Sometimes it has no color. The urine they used to test was pale yellow.

Anyway, I didn't bother asking for bloodwork to prove I was pregnant because I figured if I was showing up negative, that means I did miscarry and was long done with it. My heavy bleeding was done before I even took the tests. I had her remove my IUD in case it was causing the bleeding, and I went home.
